Ultramafic and Mafic Rocks

Dr. Ahmad Redaa

20-10-2025

1. Introduction

Ultramafic and mafic rocks represent the magnesium- and iron-rich end of the igneous spectrum.

Rock Type Silica (SiO₂ wt%) Fe–Mg Content Typical Minerals Example
Ultramafic < 45% Very high Olivine, Pyroxene Peridotite
Mafic 45–52% High Pyroxene, Plagioclase (Ca-rich) Basalt, Gabbro

2. Chemical Characteristics

Oxide Ultramafic (%) Mafic (%) Trend
SiO₂ 35–45 45–52 ↑ with differentiation
MgO 30–45 5–12 ↓ with differentiation
FeO / Fe₂O₃ 8–12 8–12 Variable
Al₂O₃ < 5 12–18 ↑ in mafic rocks
CaO 2–10 8–12 ↑ in mafic
Na₂O + K₂O < 1 2–5 ↑ strongly toward felsic

Key trend:
> From ultramafic → mafic → felsic, silica and alkalis increase; Mg, Fe, and Ca decrease.

3. Mineralogical Composition

Ultramafic Rocks

  • Dominated by ferromagnesian silicates:
    • Olivine (Fo–Fa series)
    • Orthopyroxene (Enstatite–Hypersthene)
    • Clinopyroxene (Diopside–Augite)
    • Minor spinel, chromite, or amphibole

Ultramafic Rock Types

Rock Major Minerals Texture Origin
Peridotite Olivine + Pyroxene Coarse Mantle / lower crust
Dunite >90% Olivine Granular Mantle cumulate
Harzburgite Olivine + Orthopyroxene Granular Residual mantle
Lherzolite Olivine + Opx + Cpx Equigranular Upper mantle

Mafic Rocks

  • Dominated by pyroxene and Ca-rich plagioclase, minor olivine and Fe–Ti oxides.
  • Silica-rich compared to ultramafic, typically 45–52 wt%.
Rock Major Minerals Texture Occurrence
Basalt Plagioclase + Pyroxene ± Olivine Fine-grained Extrusive (oceanic crust)
Gabbro Plagioclase + Pyroxene Coarse-grained Intrusive equivalent of basalt
Dolerite (Diabase) Plagioclase + Pyroxene Medium-grained Dike/sill intrusive
Norite / Troctolite Plagioclase + Opx / Olivine Coarse Layered intrusions

4. Formation and Tectonic Settings

Ultramafic Rocks

  • Represent mantle material or cumulates from early crystallization.
  • Primary settings:
    • Mantle peridotite (upper mantle)
    • Layered mafic–ultramafic intrusions (e.g., Bushveld, South Africa)
    • Ophiolite complexes (emplaced oceanic lithosphere)
    • Alpine-type peridotites (obducted mantle slices)

Mafic Rocks

  • Represent primary melts from partial melting of the mantle.
  • Common settings:
    • Mid-ocean ridges (MORB)
    • Island arcs (calc-alkaline basalts)
    • Intraplate settings (OIB)
    • Large igneous provinces (flood basalts)

5. Petrogenesis

  • Partial melting of mantle peridotite produces basaltic magma.
  • Fractional crystallization of basaltic magma → gabbroic cumulates.
  • Residual mantle after extraction becomes harzburgite or dunite.

Simplified sequence:

Peridotite (mantle) → Partial melt → Basalt magma → Crystallization → Gabbro cumulate

6. Ophiolite Complexes

Definition:
> A section of oceanic lithosphere and upper mantle thrust onto continental crust during plate convergence.

Significance:
Natural windows into oceanic crustal structure and mantle composition.

Ophiolite Sequence

Ophiolite sequence diagram illustrating typical oceanic crustal and upper mantle sections.

Source: Winter, J. (2014)

Unit Rock Type Description
1. Pillow lavas Basalt Submarine extrusive top layer
2. Sheeted dike complex Dolerite Vertical feeder dikes
3. Gabbroic layer Gabbro, Norite Coarse-grained intrusive rocks
4. Ultramafic cumulates Dunite, Pyroxenite Early crystallization products
5. Mantle peridotite Harzburgite, Lherzolite Residual mantle rock

Example: The Oman Ophiolite (Semail)

  • One of the best-preserved ophiolites globally.
  • Represents complete oceanic crust + upper mantle section.
  • Displays clear cumulate layering, dike complexes, and tectonic peridotite.
  • Provides insights into seafloor spreading and magma evolution.

7. Geochemical Characteristics of Ophiolitic Mafic Rocks

Setting SiO₂ (%) TiO₂ (%) FeO (%) MgO (%) Signature
MORB-type 48–52 1.5–2.5 8–12 6–10 Low-K, flat REE pattern
Island-arc type 50–55 0.5–1.0 6–10 5–8 LREE-depleted, subduction signatures
Back-arc type 50–53 1.0–2.0 7–11 6–9 Transitional MORB–arc

8. Textures and Field Relations

Texture Description Example
Cumulus texture Crystals accumulated from magma Layered gabbro
Ophitic / Subophitic Plagioclase enclosed by pyroxene Dolerite
Porphyritic Large phenocrysts in fine matrix Basalt
Serpentinization Hydration of olivine → serpentine Peridotite alteration

9. Economic Importance

  • Chromite deposits in dunites and harzburgites (layered intrusions, ophiolites)
  • Nickel–copper–PGE deposits in mafic–ultramafic complexes
  • Magnesite and asbestos from serpentinized peridotites
